items.title: Ein Haus ohne Adresse
items.dek: In Rabat finden Migrantinnen auf dem Weg nach Europa Schutz in einem Frauenhaus, das auf keiner Karte steht. Ein Blick auf die andere Seite der europäischen Grenzpolitik.
paragraphs: Wer das Frauenhaus Maison Baobab sucht, findet es auf keiner Karte. Die genaue Lage in Marokkos Hauptstadt Rabat bleibt geheim; Frauen erfahren davon nur über Beratungsstellen. Seit 2015 bietet die Einrichtung Migrantinnen und ihren Kindern einen Ort, an dem sie etwa drei Monate lang kostenlos wohnen, essen und zur Ruhe kommen können. Rund 50 Frauen und Kinder finden gleichzeitig Platz, verteilt auf drei Wohnungen.

Getragen wird das Haus von Arcom, einem Verein von Geflüchteten und Migrantengemeinschaften in Marokko. Gegründet hat ihn der Kongolese Emmanuel Mbolela, der selbst jahrelang in Marokko festsaß, bevor er 2008 in den Niederlanden Asyl erhielt. Finanziert wird die Arbeit über Spenden, unter anderem von der Hilfsorganisation Medico International. Pro Person rechnet der Verein mit etwa 75 Euro im Monat.

Die Bewohnerinnen kommen aus dem Sudan, aus Äthiopien, der Elfenbeinküste oder Gabun. Manche sind vor Krieg geflohen, andere vor einer Zwangsheirat oder vor Gewalt in der Partnerschaft. Viele haben unterwegs sexualisierte Gewalt erlebt: Einer Studie zufolge betrifft das mehr als drei Viertel der Frauen auf dieser Route. Zu den Tätern gehören Schlepper, aber auch Grenzbeamte und Polizisten.

Das Haus bietet deshalb mehr als ein Bett: medizinische Versorgung, Alphabetisierungs- und Sprachkurse in Französisch, Englisch und Arabisch, Näh- und Computerkurse und Unterricht für die Kinder. Ein Teil des Teams hat selbst Migrationserfahrung. Draußen dagegen raten die Mitarbeiterinnen zur Vorsicht, denn Razzien in den Vierteln, in denen viele Menschen aus Subsahara-Afrika leben, sind keine Seltenheit.

Der politische Rahmen ist widersprüchlich. Marokko hat kein funktionierendes nationales Asylsystem, doch die Zahl der Schutzsuchenden ist deutlich gestiegen. Beim UN-Flüchtlingshilfswerk sind über 23.000 Geflüchtete und Asylsuchende registriert; Schätzungen zur Zahl der Menschen ohne Papiere reichen bis 700.000. Zugleich zahlt die Europäische Union: Zwischen 2021 und 2023 flossen rund 193 Millionen Euro für Migrationsprogramme nach Marokko. Kritiker sprechen von einer Auslagerung der europäischen Grenzkontrolle.

Für die Frauen bleibt das Haus eine Zwischenstation. Manche wollen weiter nach Europa, obwohl sie den Weg über das Meer fürchten; andere versuchen, sich in Marokko ein Leben aufzubauen. Was die Einrichtung leisten kann, ist begrenzt. Für einige Wochen ist sie aber ein Ort, an dem niemand fragt, woher man kommt, sondern was man braucht.

glossary.en: to find some calm, settle down

items.grammar: Passive voice moved to the front for emphasis: „Getragen wird das Haus von Arcom“, „Finanziert wird die Arbeit über Spenden“. Putting the past participle first shifts the focus to who runs or funds it — a very common device in German journalism. （被动态把分词提前，强调“由谁、怎样”。）
questions: Warum bleibt die Adresse des Frauenhauses geheim?
Was kritisieren Fachleute an den Zahlungen der EU an Marokko?
Welches Angebot des Hauses halten Sie für am wichtigsten – und warum?

sources.title: taz: Frauenhaus Maison Baobab – „Hier sind sie sicher“ (9.10.2026)

paragraphs_en: Anyone looking for the Maison Baobab women's shelter won't find it on any map. Its exact location in Rabat, Morocco's capital, is kept secret; women only hear about it through counselling services. Since 2015 the shelter has offered migrant women and their children a place where they can live, eat and find some calm, free of charge, for about three months. Around 50 women and children can stay at any one time, spread across three apartments.

The house is run by Arcom, an association of refugees and migrant communities in Morocco. It was founded by Emmanuel Mbolela from Congo, who was himself stuck in Morocco for years before being granted asylum in the Netherlands in 2008. The work is funded through donations, including from the aid organisation Medico International. The association reckons on roughly 75 euros per person per month.

The residents come from Sudan, Ethiopia, Ivory Coast or Gabon. Some have fled war, others a forced marriage or violence from a partner. Many experienced sexual violence along the way: according to one study, this affects more than three quarters of the women on this route. The perpetrators include smugglers, but also border guards and police officers.

That is why the house offers more than a bed: medical care, literacy and language classes in French, English and Arabic, sewing and computer courses, and lessons for the children. Some of the team have a migration background themselves. Outside, by contrast, staff advise caution, because raids in the neighbourhoods where many people from sub-Saharan Africa live are not uncommon.

The political setting is contradictory. Morocco has no functioning national asylum system, yet the number of people seeking protection has risen sharply. More than 23,000 refugees and asylum seekers are registered with the UN refugee agency; estimates of the number of undocumented people run as high as 700,000. At the same time, the European Union pays: between 2021 and 2023, around 193 million euros went to Morocco for migration programmes. Critics speak of Europe outsourcing its border control.

For the women, the house remains a stopover. Some want to go on to Europe, even though they fear the crossing by sea; others are trying to build a life in Morocco. What the shelter can achieve is limited. But for a few weeks it is a place where nobody asks where you come from, only what you need.

items.title: Region Hannover: 3.735 Jugendliche wählen probeweise
paragraphs: Zum ersten Mal hat die Region Hannover eine U16-Wahl veranstaltet. Zwischen dem 24. August und dem 4. September konnten Kinder und Jugendliche unter 16 Jahren in 75 Wahllokalen ihre Stimme für die Regionsversammlung abgeben – symbolisch, denn das Ergebnis hatte keinen Einfluss auf die Kommunalwahl am 13. September.

Mitgemacht haben 16 der 21 Städte und Gemeinden der Region, insgesamt 3.735 junge Menschen. Die meisten waren zwischen 13 und 15 Jahre alt. In einer begleitenden, nicht repräsentativen Umfrage sagte gut die Hälfte, es sei ihnen sehr wichtig, in der Lokalpolitik gehört zu werden. Informiert hatten sie sich vor allem in der Schule.

Die Region will die Ergebnisse nun gemeinsam mit Jugendlichen auswerten und daraus neue Angebote zur Demokratiebildung entwickeln. Die Idee dahinter: Demokratie nicht nur erklären, sondern erleben lassen.

glossary.en: on a trial basis, as a mock exercise

questions: Warum war die U16-Wahl nur symbolisch?
Sollte das Wahlalter bei Kommunalwahlen sinken? Begründen Sie kurz.

sources.title: hannover.de: Erste U16-Wahl – 3.735 junge Menschen geben Stimme ab (8.10.2026)

paragraphs_en: For the first time, the Hannover region has held an under-16 election. Between 24 August and 4 September, children and teenagers under 16 could cast their vote for the regional assembly at 75 polling stations – symbolically, since the result had no effect on the local elections on 13 September.

Sixteen of the region's 21 towns and municipalities took part, with a total of 3,735 young people voting. Most of them were between 13 and 15. In an accompanying, non-representative survey, just over half said it was very important to them to be heard in local politics. They had informed themselves mainly at school.

The region now wants to evaluate the results together with young people and use them to develop new civic-education programmes. The idea behind it: don't just explain democracy, let people experience it.

items.title: Pregnant, and in detention
items.dek: One woman's months in an immigration detention centre in Texas show how little the public knows about pregnant people in ICE custody.
paragraphs: When Maria went to a routine check-in at an immigration office in Dallas in October 2025, she expected to sign a form and go home. She asked to be identified only by her first name. She was pregnant and 41 years old, she had an asylum application dating back to 2012, and she had no criminal record. Instead she was detained, and she spent roughly six months at the Bluebonnet Detention Center in Anson, a small town in West Texas.

Her account, reported this month by The Marshall Project in partnership with The 19th, is unsettling less for any single dramatic moment than for its slow accumulation of neglect. She describes meals that were cold and undercooked, prenatal vitamins that ran out for up to two weeks at a time, and nutritional drinks, prescribed by a doctor, that arrived only sporadically. Over the course of her pregnancy she developed low iron, high blood pressure and gestational diabetes, and she gained far less weight than obstetric guidelines recommend. No one, she says, gave her a plan for the birth.

In April 2026, when she was eight months pregnant, ICE released her without explanation. Her daughter was born in June. Her legal case, however, has gone against her: an immigration judge issued a removal order in the spring and her appeal was rejected in July, so every future check-in carries the possibility of being detained again.

How typical is her experience? The question is harder to answer than it should be. A 2021 ICE policy largely discourages detaining pregnant people, yet judges disagree about how binding it is. A requirement that the Department of Homeland Security publish annual figures on detained pregnant people lapsed in March 2025, and records suggest the department stopped tracking miscarriages in custody later that year. What data exist are fragments: nearly five hundred pregnant, postpartum or nursing women released from detention between early 2025 and early 2026, and more than three hundred deported in the first six weeks of 2025 alone.

Medical experts interviewed for the report stress that pregnancy raises the stakes of ordinary institutional failures. A diet that is merely unpleasant for most detainees can be dangerous for a woman who needs more calories and micronutrients, and undercooked meat carries specific risks. Advocacy groups that track pregnancies in detention describe poor nutrition as a recurring complaint rather than an exception. The department has in the past rejected allegations of mistreatment and insisted that its facilities meet high standards; ICE did not respond to the reporters' questions.

The larger issue is what a government chooses to count. A policy can look humane on paper, but without data, oversight depends on individual women being willing to tell their stories, and on journalists finding them. Maria's case is a single story. It is also a measure of how little else is known.

glossary.en: a scheduled appointment to report to immigration authorities
a legal order to deport someone
(of a rule) to expire or stop applying
in the period after giving birth

glossary.zh: 使后果更严重、风险更高
glossary.en: to make the possible consequences more serious

questions: Why does the author say the case is unsettling 'less for any single dramatic moment'?
What has made it harder to know how many pregnant people are detained?
Is personal testimony enough to drive policy change, or is data indispensable? Argue one side in three sentences.

sources.title: The Marshall Project / The 19th: The 'Nightmare' of Being Pregnant in an ICE Detention Camp (14 Oct 2026)

items.title: Onde está o Bolinha?
items.dek: O Tito ajuda a procurar um amigo.
paragraphs: Hoje é terça-feira. De manhã tem sol, mas à tarde o céu fica cinza.
A Ana está na cozinha. Ela faz um bolo de banana. A casa tem um cheiro muito bom.
De repente, alguém bate na porta: toc, toc. É a Dona Rosa. — Ana, você viu o Bolinha? Ele saiu e não voltou!
A Ana pega um guarda-chuva. O Tito olha pela janela. Começa a chover.
A Ana e a Dona Rosa procuram o Bolinha na rua. — Bolinha! Bolinha! Mas o cachorro não aparece.
O Tito sobe na janela e mia alto: miau! Ele olha para o jardim. Debaixo da árvore tem um cachorro marrom, todo molhado.
— Olha, Dona Rosa! O Tito achou o Bolinha! — diz a Ana.
O Bolinha entra na casa amarela. Ele está com frio. A Ana pega uma toalha. O Tito deita perto do cachorro.
— Agora vocês são amigos — diz a Dona Rosa, e sorri. Todos comem bolo de banana. Lá fora, a chuva continua.
paragraphs_zh: 今天是星期二。早上有太阳，可是下午天变灰了。
安娜在厨房里。她在做香蕉蛋糕。家里闻起来很香。
突然，有人敲门：咚，咚。是罗莎太太。“安娜，你看见波利尼亚了吗？它出去了，没有回来！”
安娜拿起一把雨伞。蒂托从窗户往外看。开始下雨了。
安娜和罗莎太太在街上找波利尼亚。“波利尼亚！波利尼亚！”可是狗没有出现。
蒂托爬上窗台，大声叫：喵！它看着花园。树底下有一只棕色的狗，全身湿透了。
“看，罗莎太太！蒂托找到波利尼亚了！”安娜说。
波利尼亚走进黄色的房子。它觉得冷。安娜拿来一条毛巾。蒂托躺在狗的旁边。
“现在你们是朋友了，”罗莎太太说，笑了起来。大家一起吃香蕉蛋糕。外面，雨还在下。

glossary.zh: （猫）叫 · ele mia 它喵喵叫
glossary.en: to meow · ele mia = he meows

glossary.zh: 找到（巴西常用）；也指“认为”
glossary.en: to find (common in Brazil); also 'to think'

items.grammar: estar com + noun expresses a temporary feeling: estar com frio (to be cold), estar com fome (to be hungry), estar com medo (to be afraid). Literally 'to be with cold' — unlike English 'to be cold'. （“estar com + 名词”表示一时的感觉。）
questions: O que a Ana faz na cozinha?
paragraphs_en: Today is Tuesday. In the morning it's sunny, but in the afternoon the sky turns grey.
Ana is in the kitchen. She's making a banana cake. The house smells really good.
Suddenly someone knocks on the door: knock, knock. It's Dona Rosa. "Ana, have you seen Bolinha? He went out and didn't come back!"
Ana grabs an umbrella. Tito looks out of the window. It starts to rain.
Ana and Dona Rosa look for Bolinha in the street. "Bolinha! Bolinha!" But the dog doesn't appear.
Tito climbs onto the window and meows loudly: meow! He looks at the garden. Under the tree there's a brown dog, soaking wet.
"Look, Dona Rosa! Tito found Bolinha!" says Ana.
Bolinha comes into the yellow house. He's cold. Ana gets a towel. Tito lies down next to the dog.
"Now you two are friends," says Dona Rosa, and smiles. Everyone eats banana cake. Outside, the rain keeps falling.

items.title: Na feira
paragraphs: Ana: Bom dia! Quanto custa o quilo da banana?
Feirante: Bom dia! O quilo custa seis reais.
Ana: Está bom. Eu quero dois quilos, por favor.
Feirante: Dois quilos de banana. Mais alguma coisa?
Ana: Tem manga?
Feirante: Tem, sim. Estão bem doces hoje. É três por dez reais.
Ana: Então eu quero três mangas.
Feirante: Pronto. Banana e manga: são vinte e dois reais.
Ana: Posso pagar com Pix?
Feirante: Pode, claro. A chave está aqui na placa.
Ana: Pronto, paguei. Obrigada!
Feirante: Eu que agradeço. Até a semana que vem!
paragraphs_zh: 安娜：早上好！香蕉一公斤多少钱？
摊主：早上好！一公斤六雷亚尔。
安娜：好的。我要两公斤，谢谢。
摊主：两公斤香蕉。还要别的吗？
安娜：有芒果吗？
摊主：有的。今天特别甜。三个十雷亚尔。
安娜：那我要三个芒果。
摊主：好了。香蕉和芒果，一共二十二雷亚尔。
安娜：可以用 Pix 付吗？
摊主：当然可以。收款码就在这块牌子上。
安娜：好了，付好了。谢谢！
摊主：是我该谢谢你。下周见！

glossary.en: thank YOU (lit. 'I'm the one who thanks')

items.grammar: In spoken Brazilian Portuguese, tem is the usual way to say 'there is / do you have': Tem manga? (Do you have mangoes?) – Tem, sim. It sounds more natural than há. （巴西口语常用 tem 表示“有”。）
questions: Quanto custa o quilo da banana?
paragraphs_en: Ana: Good morning! How much is a kilo of bananas?
Stallholder: Good morning! A kilo is six reais.
Ana: Fine. I'd like two kilos, please.
Stallholder: Two kilos of bananas. Anything else?
Ana: Do you have mangoes?
Stallholder: Yes, we do. They're really sweet today. It's three for ten reais.
Ana: Then I'll take three mangoes.
Stallholder: There you go. Bananas and mangoes: that's twenty-two reais.
Ana: Can I pay with Pix?
Stallholder: Of course. The key is here on the sign.
Ana: Done, I've paid. Thank you!
Stallholder: Thank you! See you next week!

items.title: Lesetipps für heute
items.dek: Fünf Texte zum Selberlesen: Kommentar, Reportage, Sprache.

picks.title: Berlin auf dem Weg zur Vergesellschaftung: Ein Triumph für die Linken – mit ungewissem Ausgang
picks.author: Daniel Böldt
picks.zh: 评论：柏林三党同意把万套以上的大房企收归公有。作者认为时间表、诉讼和补偿上限都悬而未决，短期内对房租的影响也有限。
picks.en: Comment: Berlin's three parties agree to take large landlords (10,000+ flats) into public ownership. The author argues the timetable, lawsuits and compensation cap are all unresolved, and the short-term effect on rents is limited.

picks.title: Protest statt Physiktest
picks.zh: 柏林学生封锁两所学校，抗议教育经费削减和联邦国防军进校园。
picks.en: Berlin students blockade two schools to protest education cuts and the army's presence in schools.

picks.title: Solidarisches Rudelgucken
picks.zh: 女子体育热潮：Honeyball Club 为女性和性少数群体组织公开观赛。
picks.en: The boom in women's sport: the Honeyball Club organises public screenings for women and queer fans.

picks.title: An der Toleranzgrenze
picks.zh: 荷兰青少年对同性恋的接受度明显下降。记者走进一所学校，看能做些什么。
picks.en: Acceptance of homosexuality among Dutch teenagers has dropped sharply; a reporter visits a school to see what can be done.

picks.title: Na, wie sprichst du denn?
picks.zh: 为什么奥地利人和德国人有时互相听不懂？德语变体的入门读物。
picks.en: Why Austrians and Germans sometimes don't understand each other – an introduction to the varieties of German.

items.title: Today's reading list
items.dek: Six pieces worth reading in full, from science to economics. Open them on the original sites.

picks.title: How Tree Rings Challenged the Myth of American Wilderness
picks.author: M. R. O'Connor
picks.zh: 树木年轮里的火疤显示：欧洲殖民者眼中“未经开垦的荒野”，其实早被原住民用火长期管理。科学与历史叙事交织的长文。（经 Longreads 推荐）
picks.en: Fire scars in tree rings show that the 'untouched wilderness' European settlers described had long been managed with fire by Indigenous peoples. Science and history woven together. (Via Longreads.)

picks.title: Bitch: a history
picks.author: Karen Stollznow
picks.zh: 一个词的变迁史：它怎样在词性、动物和性别之间游走，又折射出性别与权力的关系。语言学加性别研究。
picks.en: The life story of one word – how it moved between animals, insults and reclamation, and what that reveals about gender and power. Linguistics meets gender studies.

picks.title: Methodical banality
picks.author: Hannah Katznelson
picks.zh: 把 16 世纪伊拉斯谟等人文主义者“批量生产文章”的方法，和今天的大语言模型放在一起比较。
picks.en: Compares how Renaissance humanists like Erasmus mass-produced texts from templates with today's large language models.

picks.title: What the West can learn from AI optimists in the rest of the world
picks.author: Payal Arora
picks.zh: 作者认为，西方对 AI 多是焦虑，而许多发展中国家的人更看重它的实际好处；资源有限反而逼出了更务实的用法。
picks.en: Argues that while the West is mostly anxious about AI, many people in the Global South focus on practical benefits – scarcity breeds pragmatism.

picks.title: Tax the Rich and Slash the Military Budget
picks.author: Nancy Folbre
picks.zh: 女性主义经济学家 Folbre 论证：对财富和资本按工资同等税率征税、削减军费，就能为美国的全民托育、全民医保和社会住房买单。
picks.en: Feminist economist Folbre argues that taxing wealth and capital at the same rates as wages, and cutting military spending, could pay for universal childcare, healthcare and social housing in the US.

picks.title: A Blood-Red Tide
picks.author: Andre Pagliarini
picks.zh: 巴西大选首轮弗拉维奥·博索纳罗领先卢拉。作者把它放进拉美整体右转的背景里，同时认为卢拉的执政成绩被低估了。正好配合你学葡语。
picks.en: Flávio Bolsonaro leads Lula in the first round of Brazil's election. The author places this in Latin America's broader rightward turn, while arguing Lula's record is underrated. Good context for your Portuguese.

picks.title: The Long Read – latest essays
picks.zh: Guardian 的长文专栏，每个工作日一篇，涵盖社会、科学、经济和国际议题。去原网站挑一篇读完，喜欢的可以粘进「我的文章」细读。
picks.en: The Guardian's long-read series. Pick one on the site and read it to the end; paste it into 'My articles' if you want to study it.

picks.title: Ideas – essays and arguments
picks.zh: The Atlantic 的评论和思想随笔栏目。去原网站挑一篇读完，喜欢的可以粘进「我的文章」细读。
picks.en: The Atlantic's essays and arguments. Pick one on the site and read it to the end; paste it into 'My articles' if you want to study it.
